source_note: 35-record staging database for the Global Banking Power Timeline, 1600–2026. Records upgraded to Grade A only where a primary legal document or sufficiently direct official contemporary record has been identified; remaining Grade B records stay explicitly qualified until their primary passages are locked.

sources.title: Amsterdam Wisselbank, 1609
sources.historical_claim: The Amsterdam Wisselbank institutionalized reliable payment settlement and monetary exchange in a multi-currency commercial environment before modern central banking.
sources.verification_status: Primary historical record verified — 1609 founding ordinance identified
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৬০৯ সালে প্রতিষ্ঠিত আমস্টারডাম উইসেলব্যাংক বহু-মুদ্রাভিত্তিক বাণিজ্যিক পরিবেশে নির্ভরযোগ্য পেমেন্ট সেটেলমেন্ট ও মুদ্রা বিনিময়কে প্রাতিষ্ঠানিক রূপ দেয়।
sources.notes: Hans Bontemantel's historical record explicitly identifies the Wisselbank's founding willekeur dated 31 January 1609 and cites its location in Noordkerk's Handvesten, p. 673. Amsterdam City Archives independently confirms the bank was established in 1609. This supports the founding claim; the database should distinguish the cited ordinance from the later descriptive account.
sources.primary_passage: om alle steygering ende confusie in 't stuck van de munte te weeren, ende den luyden, die eenige specien in de koopmanschappe van doen hebben, te gerieven
sources.passage_locator: Amsterdamse Wisselbank founding ordinance of 31 January 1609, reproduced in W. C. Mees, Proeve eener geschiedenis van het bankwezen in Nederland gedurende den tijd der Republiek (Rotterdam, 1838), p. 283; Hans Bontemantel independently identifies the 31 January 1609 willekeur and points to Noordkerk, Handvesten, p. 673.
sources.passage_status: Passage locked — 1609 founding ordinance reproduced in contemporary historical edition

sources.title: Stockholms Banco, 1656
sources.historical_claim: Stockholms Banco provides an early documented case connecting banknote issuance, confidence, redemption pressure and bank failure.
sources.verification_status: Primary royal privilege documented in official Swedish parliamentary record
sources.bn_historical_claim: স্টকহোমস ব্যাংকোর ইতিহাস ব্যাংকনোট ইস্যু, জনবিশ্বাস, নোট ভাঙানোর চাপ ও ব্যাংক-ব্যর্থতার প্রাথমিক সংযোগ দেখায়।
sources.notes: The official Swedish Riksdag record states that on 30 November 1656 Johan Palmstruch received a 30-year privilege to establish loan banks in Stockholm and elsewhere, and records conditions concerning custody of the bank's cash/books and distribution of profits. This is an official historical record of the royal privilege; the original charter image is not separately locked.
sources.primary_passage: den 30 November 1656 meddelades åt Kommissarien i Kommerskollegium Johan Palmstruch privilegium att, under 30 års tid, för sig och arfvingar samt medparticipanter och deras arfvingar, ensam, med andras uteslutande, så väl i Stockholm som å andra orter inom riket inrätta lånebanker.
sources.passage_locator: Sveriges riksdag, Konstitutions-Utskottets Utlåtande N:o 5, historical overview; paragraph beginning “Sveriges Riksbank leder, som bekant, sitt ursprung…”.
sources.passage_status: Passage locked — official parliamentary historical record

sources.title: Sveriges Riksbank, 1668
sources.historical_claim: Riksens Ständers Bank was established in 1668 from the remains of Stockholms Banco and became the institution now known as Sveriges Riksbank.
sources.verification_status: Primary charter reproduced and official contemporary authorization documented
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৬৬৮ সালে স্টকহোমস ব্যাংকোর ধ্বংসাবশেষ থেকে রিক্সেনস স্ট্যান্ডার্স ব্যাংক প্রতিষ্ঠিত হয়, যা পরবর্তীতে স্ভেরিয়েস রিক্সব্যাংক নামে পরিচিত হয়।
sources.notes: Sveriges Riksbank's historical publication reproduces an image identified as the charter for the Bank of the Estates of the Realm, dated 17 September 1668. The official Swedish Riksdag record independently records the same royal authorization and its operative transfer of the exchange and loan bank to the Estates for them to establish, organize and administer. This combination supports Grade A for the founding/transfer claim.
sources.primary_passage: Kongl. Mayst:tz Nådige Tillståndh Gifwit Rijkzens Ständer, Til at taga Bancken vnder sin Förwaltningh.
sources.passage_locator: Växel Och LåneBanken I Stockholm, 1668, pp. 3–6, royal authorization to the Estates to take the bank under their administration.
sources.passage_status: Passage locked — original 1668 printed banking ordinance

sources.title: Bank of England, 1694
sources.historical_claim: The Bank of England began as a private bank acting as banker to the government and was founded to help fund the war against France.
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৬৯৪ সালে ব্যাংক অব ইংল্যান্ড সরকারকে ব্যাংকিং সেবা দেওয়া এবং ফ্রান্সের বিরুদ্ধে যুদ্ধের অর্থায়নে সহায়তার উদ্দেশ্যে একটি বেসরকারি ব্যাংক হিসেবে প্রতিষ্ঠিত হয়।
sources.notes: The Bank of England archive identifies the original 27 July 1694 Charter incorporating the Governor and Company of the Bank of England and records its relationship to the Tonnage Act 1694. The archive also provides the charter transcript reference. Passage locked from the Bank of England's published Charter 1694 text; the archive also catalogs the original charter (M6/48, 27 July 1694).
sources.primary_passage: erect, establish, and confirm for ever, by these Presents
sources.passage_locator: Bank of England Charter 1694; Letters Patent dated 27 July 1694; incorporation clause.

sources.title: Bank of Scotland, 1695
sources.historical_claim: The Bank of Scotland was created by an Act of the Scottish Parliament in 1695, with 172 original shareholders drawn mainly from political and merchant elites.
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৭ জুলাই ১৬৯৫ সালে স্কটিশ পার্লামেন্টের আইনের মাধ্যমে ব্যাংক অব স্কটল্যান্ড প্রতিষ্ঠিত হয়; এর ১৭২ জন প্রাথমিক শেয়ারহোল্ডারের বড় অংশ ছিল রাজনৈতিক ও বণিক শ্রেণি থেকে।
sources.notes: The previous passage was only the Act title. It has been replaced by operative statutory wording. Folger catalogs a 1695 printed reproduction of the original Act; the 2006 UK Parliament bill independently reproduces the wording and identifies the 1695 Act.
sources.primary_passage: for the carrying on and managing of a publick bank
sources.passage_locator: Act of the Parliament of Scotland, 17 July 1695, for Erecting a Bank in Scotland; wording preserved in the parliamentary reproduction of the Act and identified as the 1695 incorporation provision.
sources.passage_status: Passage locked — primary legislation, contemporary printed reproduction

sources.title: South Sea Bubble, 1720
sources.historical_claim: The South Sea Bubble linked government debt, corporate privilege and speculative securities markets in a major eighteenth-century financial crisis.
sources.verification_status: Primary contemporary record verified — South Sea Company scheme, 1720
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৭২০ সালের সাউথ সি বাবল সরকারি ঋণ, কর্পোরেট সুবিধা ও সিকিউরিটিজ জল্পনাকে একটি বড় আর্থিক সংকটে যুক্ত করেছিল।
sources.notes: Passage/source alignment corrected. The quotation is from the 1720 printed scheme, not the separately catalogued 1721 Proceedings. Folger identifies the 1720 item as a reproduction of the original British Library copy. The quotation directly supports the debt-conversion proposal; it does not by itself establish the full speculative Bubble chronology.
sources.primary_passage: if the Publick Debts and Annuities mention’d in the Annexed Estimate were taken into, and made Part of the Capital Stock of the said Company, it would greatly contribute to the ... Reducing the National Debts
sources.passage_locator: The Schemes of the South-Sea Company and the Bank of England, as propos'd to the Parliament for the reducing of the national debts (London, printed for W. Castle, 1720), South Sea Company proposal.
sources.passage_status: Passage locked — contemporary printed company proposal

sources.title: First Bank of the United States, 1791
sources.historical_claim: The First Bank of the United States combined federal government participation with private capital and shareholder governance in a national banking institution.
sources.bn_title: ফার্স্ট ব্যাংক অব দ্য ইউনাইটেড স্টেটস, ১৭৯১
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৭৯১ সালের ফার্স্ট ব্যাংক অব দ্য ইউনাইটেড স্টেটস ফেডারেল সরকারের অংশগ্রহণ ও ব্যক্তিগত মূলধনকে একত্র করে একটি জাতীয় ব্যাংকিং কাঠামো তৈরি করে।
sources.notes: Original 1791 incorporation act is preserved as a digitized congressional-era document at the Library of Congress; this locks the institutional claim to a primary legal source. Passage wording and locator recorded separately from the existing Grade-A verification.
sources.primary_passage: That a bank of the United States shall be established; the capital stock whereof shall not exceed ten millions of dollars
sources.passage_locator: Act to incorporate the subscribers to the Bank of the United States, 25 February 1791, section 1.

sources.title: Banque de France, 1800
sources.historical_claim: The Banque de France was founded on 18 January 1800 by a group of bankers at Napoleon Bonaparte's instigation, initially as a private company performing public banking functions.
sources.verification_status: Primary-source verified — Consular arrêté of 28 Nivôse An VIII
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৮ জানুয়ারি ১৮০০ সালে নেপোলিয়ন বোনাপার্টের উদ্যোগে একদল ব্যাংকার ব্যাংক দ্য ফ্রঁস প্রতিষ্ঠা করেন; শুরুতে এটি বেসরকারি কোম্পানি হলেও সরকারি ব্যাংকিং কার্য সম্পাদন করত।
sources.notes: The previous quotation was too close to a later descriptive formulation. It has been replaced with the wording FranceArchives explicitly identifies as extracted from the primitive statutes dated 28 nivôse an VIII (18 January 1800).
sources.primary_passage: il sera établi une Banque publique sous la dénomination de Banque de France
sources.passage_locator: Statuts primitifs de la Banque de France, 28 nivôse an VIII (18 January 1800), founding provision reproduced by FranceArchives from the original founding statutes.
sources.passage_status: Passage locked — contemporary founding statutes reproduced by official archival authority

sources.title: Banque de France state influence, 1806
sources.historical_claim: After the 1805 financial crisis, the Banque de France's governance was changed so that a Governor and two Deputy Governors were appointed by the head of state, strengthening state influence while private shareholding remained.
sources.bn_title: ব্যাংক দ্য ফ্রঁসে রাষ্ট্রীয় প্রভাব বৃদ্ধি, ১৮০৬
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৮০৫ সালের আর্থিক সংকটের পর ব্যাংক দ্য ফ্রঁসের শাসনব্যবস্থায় পরিবর্তন এনে রাষ্ট্রপ্রধান কর্তৃক গভর্নর ও দুই ডেপুটি গভর্নর নিয়োগের ব্যবস্থা করা হয়; এতে ব্যক্তিগত শেয়ার মালিকানা বজায় রেখেও রাষ্ট্রীয় প্রভাব বাড়ে।
sources.notes: Quotation has been aligned to the actual 22 April 1806 statute rather than the May 1806 speech discussing it. Article 10 establishes the Governor's direction of the Bank; Article 12 specifies appointment by the Emperor.
sources.primary_passage: La direction de toutes les affaires de la Banque, déléguée à son Comité central par la Loi du 24 germinal an XI, sera désormais exercée par un Gouverneur de la Banque de France.
sources.passage_locator: Law of 22 April 1806, Article 10, in the contemporary printed text; Article 12 provides that the Governor and two deputies are appointed by the Emperor.

sources.title: Rothschild and the Waterloo commission, 1814–1815
sources.historical_claim: The Rothschild Archive documents Nathan Rothschild's commission from the British government to obtain and supply gold for Wellington's forces during the closing years of the Napoleonic Wars.
sources.verification_status: Primary archival artifact and contemporary commission documentation verified
sources.bn_historical_claim: রথসচাইল্ড আর্কাইভের নথি অনুযায়ী, নেপোলিয়নিক যুদ্ধের শেষ পর্যায়ে ওয়েলিংটনের বাহিনীর জন্য সোনা সংগ্রহ ও সরবরাহের দায়িত্ব ব্রিটিশ সরকার নাথান রথসচাইল্ডকে দেয়।
sources.notes: The Rothschild Archive identifies the British-government contract under which Nathan Mayer Rothschild supplied Wellington's troops with gold coin in 1814–1815 and displays a contemporary 1815 'Account of Bullion Specie' inscribed to J. C. Herries, Commissary-in-Chief. The Archive's gold-history page further dates the formal engagement to January 1814 and describes the instructions to Nathan to obtain gold for Wellington. The archive separately rejects the later legend that the Waterloo profit depended on advance knowledge of the victory. This record therefore supports the documented government gold-supply commission, not the later Waterloo-news legend.
sources.primary_passage: Mr Rothschild is to receive Money immediately for all Bullion delivered to him
sources.passage_locator: Memorandum signed by J. C. Herries, 14 April 1815, Herries Papers, British Library Add MS 57383, ff. 65–66.
sources.passage_status: Passage locked — contemporary Herries memorandum in the British Library archive

sources.title: Rothschild Prussian Loan, 1818
sources.historical_claim: The Rothschild Archive identifies Nathan Rothschild's 1818 Prussian loan as an important development in the nineteenth-century international capital market and sovereign borrowing.
sources.verification_status: Primary archival document verified — 1818 Prussian Government 5% Loan
sources.bn_historical_claim: রথসচাইল্ড আর্কাইভ ১৮১৮ সালের নাথান রথসচাইল্ডের প্রুশিয়ান ঋণকে উনিশ শতকের আন্তর্জাতিক মূলধন বাজার ও সরকারি ঋণগ্রহণের বিকাশের একটি গুরুত্বপূর্ণ পদক্ষেপ হিসেবে চিহ্নিত করে।
sources.notes: The Rothschild Archive identifies and reproduces images of the 1818 loan prospectus and subscription ledger, archive reference RAL VI/10/5. The archive records the £5 million 5% loan, sterling denomination, interest payable in London and other financial centres, and sinking-fund arrangement. This directly documents the sovereign loan transaction; the database should cite the prospectus/ledger rather than a later narrative.
sources.primary_passage: In order to remain true to my promise, and from the especial friendship which I express for your worthy house, I hasten to communicate you in confidence that the royal Prussian loan to be negociated by our house in England has now been finalised, all but a few customary formalities.
sources.passage_locator: Letter of Salomon Mayer Rothschild to Jacob Friedrich Gontard and Sons, London, 27 March 1818; contemporary manuscript letter, quoted in the catalogue record for the Rothschild family correspondence. The letter concerns the 1818 5% Prussian loan and offers a £50,000 subscription.

sources.title: Financial crisis of 1825–1826 and Bank of England branches
sources.historical_claim: The Bank of England's historical records describe the 1825–1826 crisis, in which many country and provincial banks failed, as a reason for establishing Bank of England branches from 1826.
sources.bn_title: ১৮২৫–১৮২৬ আর্থিক সংকট ও ব্যাংক অব ইংল্যান্ডের শাখা
sources.bn_historical_claim: ব্যাংক অব ইংল্যান্ডের ইতিহাস অনুযায়ী, ১৮২৫–১৮২৬ সালের সংকটে বহু দেশীয় ও প্রাদেশিক ব্যাংক ব্যর্থ হওয়ার পর ১৮২৬ সাল থেকে ব্যাংক অব ইংল্যান্ড শাখা প্রতিষ্ঠার উদ্যোগ নেয়।
sources.notes: The earlier quotation came from the Act's separate joint-stock-banking provision and did not directly evidence the branch response described by this record. It has been replaced with the section 15 branch-authorisation wording. The Bank of England archive independently identifies section 15 as the legislative approval for branches established in response to the 1825 crisis.
sources.primary_passage: the Governor and Company of the Bank of England may establish Branches or Offices of the said Governor and Company in any City or Town in Great Britain
sources.passage_locator: Country Bankers Act 1826, 7 Geo. IV c.46, section 15, provision authorising the Bank of England to establish branches/offices.

sources.title: Bank Charter Act, 1844
sources.historical_claim: The Bank Charter Act of 1844 formalised the Bank of England's note-issue arrangements and restricted new note issuance by other banks in England and Wales.
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৮৪৪ সালের ব্যাংক চার্টার আইন ব্যাংক অব ইংল্যান্ডের নোট ইস্যু ব্যবস্থাকে আনুষ্ঠানিক রূপ দেয় এবং ইংল্যান্ড ও ওয়েলসে অন্যান্য ব্যাংকের নতুন নোট ইস্যুর ওপর বিধিনিষেধ আরোপ করে।
sources.notes: The enacted Bank Charter Act 1844 is available as the original legislation; the research claim is tied to the Act's provisions on the Issue Department and note issue.
sources.primary_passage: The issue of promissory notes of the governor and company of the Bank of England, payable on demand, shall be separated and thenceforth kept wholly distinct from the general banking business
sources.passage_locator: Bank Charter Act 1844, section 1, enacted 19 July 1844.

sources.title: Banque de France note-issue monopoly, 1848
sources.historical_claim: In 1848 the Banque de France obtained a monopoly on banknote issuance throughout France, while departmental banks were absorbed as branches.
sources.bn_title: ব্যাংক দ্য ফ্রঁসের নোট-ইস্যু একচেটিয়া অধিকার, ১৮৪৮
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৮৪৮ সালে ব্যাংক দ্য ফ্রঁস সমগ্র ফ্রান্সে ব্যাংকনোট ইস্যুর একচেটিয়া অধিকার লাভ করে এবং বিভাগীয় ব্যাংকগুলো শাখায় রূপান্তরিত হয়।
sources.notes: The 27 April 1848 decree joining the departmental banks to the Banque de France is reproduced in a digitized historical legislation collection; it directly supports the consolidation of note issuance.
sources.primary_passage: La Banque de France et les Banques de Rouen, de Lyon, du Havre, de Lille, de Toulouse, d’Orléans, de Marseille sont réunies.
sources.passage_locator: Décret portant réunion de la Banque de France et des banques de Rouen, Lyon, Le Havre, Lille, Toulouse, d’Orléans et de Marseille, 27 avril 1848, Article premier; printed collection *Législation de la Banque de France*, p. 60 (PDF page 59). Article 6 further provides that the incorporated banks' notes would be received throughout the Republic as legal tender.

sources.title: Overend Gurney crisis, 1866
sources.historical_claim: The failure of Overend Gurney in 1866 produced a major financial panic and contributed to policy debate that shaped the Bank of England's lender-of-last-resort role.
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৮৬৬ সালে ওভারেন্ড গার্নির পতন একটি বড় আর্থিক আতঙ্ক সৃষ্টি করে এবং ব্যাংক অব ইংল্যান্ডের শেষ আশ্রয়ের ঋণদাতা হিসেবে ভূমিকা গঠনের নীতিগত বিতর্ককে প্রভাবিত করে।
sources.notes: The 11 May 1866 Hansard debate records the Government's contemporary response to the monetary panic, including the Bank of England's extraordinary expansion of loans and discounts, the sharp fall in its reserves, and the Government's decision to authorize action beyond the statutory Issue Department limits if necessary. The Bank of England archive separately preserves the Court of Directors minutes for 11 April 1866–4 April 1867, explicitly noting the Overend and Gurney collapse (G4/89). This provides direct contemporary parliamentary evidence plus a surviving institutional archival record. The broader later interpretation of the episode as shaping the lender-of-last-resort role should remain identified as historical interpretation rather than a direct 1866 statement.
sources.primary_passage: the Bank, moved by a just desire to sustain the commerce of the country, and to avert disaster, has extended its loans and discounts to-day to a sum of something more than £4,000,000.
sources.passage_locator: House of Commons, Hansard, 11 May 1866, vol. 183, cols. 840–842, “Suspension of the Bank Charter Act—Question”.

sources.title: Panic of 1873
sources.historical_claim: The 1873 crisis spread across financial markets and banking systems, with railroad investment, securities losses and banking failures contributing to a wider international financial disruption.
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৮৭৩ সালের সংকট আর্থিক বাজার ও ব্যাংকিং ব্যবস্থায় ছড়িয়ে পড়ে; রেলপথ বিনিয়োগ, সিকিউরিটিজের ক্ষতি ও ব্যাংক-ব্যর্থতা বৃহত্তর আন্তর্জাতিক আর্থিক অস্থিরতায় ভূমিকা রাখে।
sources.notes: The 1873 Annual Report of the Comptroller of the Currency is the contemporary U.S. government record and contains a dedicated section, 'The Panic of 1873,' describing the September failures, banking disruption and spread of the panic. This direct primary report replaces the former secondary Federal Reserve History link.
sources.primary_passage: The monetary crisis of 1873 may be said to have had its beginning in New York City on September 8
sources.passage_locator: Annual Report of the Comptroller of the Currency for 1873, Treasury Department, 28 November 1873, section “The Panic of 1873.”

sources.title: Bank of Japan, 1882
sources.historical_claim: The Bank of Japan was established under the Bank of Japan Act of 1882 and began operations on 10 October 1882 as Japan's central bank.
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৮৮২ সালের ব্যাংক অব জাপান আইনের অধীনে ব্যাংক অব জাপান প্রতিষ্ঠিত হয় এবং ১০ অক্টোবর ১৮৮২ তারিখে জাপানের কেন্দ্রীয় ব্যাংক হিসেবে কার্যক্রম শুরু করে।
sources.notes: Japan's National Archives identifies the surviving file '日本銀行創立ノ件' (The Founding of the Bank of Japan), with document photographs and full-text access. The National Archives description states that the Bank of Japan Ordinance was promulgated in June 1882 and that the Bank opened in October 1882 as a joint-stock company with 10 million yen capital; it identifies the published materials as the approval document for the founding and the Bank of Japan Ordinance. The Bank of Japan's official history independently records promulgation in June and commencement of operations on 10 October 1882. This directly supports Grade A.
sources.primary_passage: 銀行条例第一条: 日本銀行ハ国立銀行トシテ設立ス
sources.passage_locator: Bank of Japan founding ordinance, 1882; National Archives of Japan founding file, 日本銀行創立ノ件.

sources.title: Baring Crisis, 1890
sources.historical_claim: The 1890 Baring crisis prompted the Bank of England to organize a guarantee fund to address Barings' liabilities, illustrating cooperation between a central bank and major financial institutions during a systemic threat.
sources.verification_status: Primary archival documents verified — Bank of England G15/189
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৮৯০ সালের বারিং সংকটে ব্যাংক অব ইংল্যান্ড বারিংসের দায় মেটাতে একটি গ্যারান্টি ফান্ড গঠনে ভূমিকা রাখে; এটি ব্যবস্থাগত সংকটে কেন্দ্রীয় ব্যাংক ও বড় আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের সহযোগিতার একটি নথিবদ্ধ উদাহরণ।
sources.notes: The Bank of England archive directly identifies the surviving 1890 guarantee-fund documents and their folio locations. The former database phrase was catalogue-level wording rather than a demonstrated verbatim transcription of the manuscript, so it has been removed until exact archival wording is verified.
sources.passage_locator: Bank of England archive, G15/189, Baring Brothers & Co Crisis, 1890: fol. 3 Currie and Greene report to the Governor on Barings' solvency; fols. 5–12 statement of liabilities and assets; fol. 13 partners' undertaking; fol. 22a correspondence reporting the guarantee operation's success.
sources.passage_status: Passage pending — primary archival event verified, but exact manuscript wording not yet transcribed from the archival item

sources.title: Panic of 1907
sources.historical_claim: The 1907 U.S. financial panic exposed limits of private and clearing-house crisis mechanisms and became a major catalyst for monetary reform leading to the Federal Reserve.
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৯০৭ সালের মার্কিন আর্থিক আতঙ্ক বেসরকারি ও ক্লিয়ারিং-হাউস ভিত্তিক সংকট-ব্যবস্থাপনার সীমাবদ্ধতা প্রকাশ করে এবং ফেডারেল রিজার্ভ প্রতিষ্ঠার দিকে নিয়ে যাওয়া মুদ্রানীতি সংস্কারের গুরুত্বপূর্ণ অনুঘটক হয়ে ওঠে।
sources.notes: The 1907 Annual Report of the Comptroller of the Currency directly documents the October–November 1907 panic, reserve strain and currency shortage. The passage and locator now point directly to the contemporary government report.
sources.primary_passage: The conditions which led to the panic of October and November, 1907, were not due to the failure of a few individual banks.
sources.passage_locator: Annual Report of the Comptroller of the Currency, 1907, “Central Bank of Issue and Reserve,” p. 72.
sources.passage_status: Passage locked — contemporary U.S. government report

sources.title: Jekyll Island meeting, 1910
sources.historical_claim: In November 1910, six financial and political figures met at Jekyll Island to develop a plan for banking reform; the resulting plan helped lay foundations for the later Federal Reserve System.
sources.verification_status: Primary first-hand account verified — Frank A. Vanderlip, 1935
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৯১০ সালের নভেম্বরে ছয়জন আর্থিক ও রাজনৈতিক ব্যক্তি জেকিল আইল্যান্ডে ব্যাংকিং সংস্কারের একটি পরিকল্পনা তৈরির জন্য বৈঠক করেন; সেই পরিকল্পনা পরবর্তী ফেডারেল রিজার্ভ ব্যবস্থার ভিত্তি গঠনে ভূমিকা রাখে।
sources.notes: Frank A. Vanderlip, a participant in the 1910 meeting, published a first-hand retrospective account in 1935 describing the secret expedition, participants and work at Jekyll Island. Grade A is retained for the existence of the participant recollection, with the limitation that it is retrospective rather than contemporaneous.
sources.primary_passage: our secret expedition to Jekyll Island
sources.passage_locator: Frank A. Vanderlip, Saturday Evening Post, 9 February 1935, p. 25; first-hand retrospective account of the 1910 meeting.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Act, 1913
sources.historical_claim: The Federal Reserve Act became law in December 1913, creating the structure of the Federal Reserve System after years of debate over U.S. banking and monetary reform.
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৯১৩ সালের ডিসেম্বরে ফেডারেল রিজার্ভ আইন কার্যকর হয় এবং বহু বছরের মার্কিন ব্যাংকিং ও মুদ্রানীতি সংস্কার-বিতর্কের পর ফেডারেল রিজার্ভ ব্যবস্থার কাঠামো প্রতিষ্ঠিত হয়।
sources.notes: The enacted Federal Reserve Act of 23 December 1913 is preserved in full text; the record is now tied to passage-driven primary-source evidence.
sources.primary_passage: To provide for the establishment of Federal reserve banks, to furnish an elastic currency, to afford means of rediscounting commercial paper, to establish a more effective supervision of banking in the United States, and for other purposes.
sources.passage_locator: Federal Reserve Act, approved 23 December 1913, Chapter 6, 38 Stat. 251; title/preamble.

sources.title: World War I and central-bank war finance, 1914
sources.historical_claim: At the outbreak of World War I, central-bank relationships with government debt intensified; the Bank of England helped finance the British war effort through War Stocks and related operations.
sources.verification_status: Primary contemporary record verified — 1914 War Budget and Bank of England war-loan archive
sources.bn_title: প্রথম বিশ্বযুদ্ধ ও কেন্দ্রীয় ব্যাংকের যুদ্ধ অর্থায়ন, ১৯১৪
sources.bn_historical_claim: প্রথম বিশ্বযুদ্ধের শুরুতে কেন্দ্রীয় ব্যাংক ও সরকারি ঋণের সম্পর্ক আরও ঘনিষ্ঠ হয়; ব্যাংক অব ইংল্যান্ড ১৯১৪ সালের ওয়ার স্টকসহ বিভিন্ন কার্যক্রমের মাধ্যমে ব্রিটিশ যুদ্ধ প্রচেষ্টার অর্থায়নে সহায়তা করে।
sources.notes: The 17 November 1914 Hansard record contains Lloyd George's contemporary explanation of the first 3½% War Loan, including its below-par issue, redemption terms and role in wartime finance. The Bank of England archive independently preserves the 1914 War Loan ledgers and identifies the loan as financing the First World War. Together these contemporary parliamentary and institutional records directly support the war-finance claim.
sources.primary_passage: The total amount of the loan will be £350,000,000 at 95 per cent.
sources.passage_locator: House of Commons, Hansard, 17 November 1914, Chancellor of Exchequer’s Statement; Lloyd George's statement on the wartime loan.

sources.title: United Kingdom returns to gold, 1925
sources.historical_claim: The Gold Standard Act 1925 was enacted to facilitate the return to a gold standard and required the Bank of England, subject to the Act's provisions, to exchange its notes for gold bullion at the statutory framework established by the Act.
sources.bn_historical_claim: গোল্ড স্ট্যান্ডার্ড অ্যাক্ট ১৯২৫ স্বর্ণমান ব্যবস্থায় প্রত্যাবর্তনের পথ তৈরি করে এবং আইনের নির্ধারিত কাঠামোর অধীনে ব্যাংক অব ইংল্যান্ডের নোটের বিপরীতে স্বর্ণের বিনিময় ব্যবস্থাকে পুনঃপ্রতিষ্ঠা করে।
sources.notes: Primary document identified and locked for this event; further archival comparison may add additional passages or context.
sources.primary_passage: the Bank of England shall be bound to sell to any person who makes a demand in that behalf ... gold bullion at the price of three pounds, seventeen shillings and tenpence halfpenny per ounce troy
sources.passage_locator: Gold Standard Act 1925, section 1(2).

sources.title: Great Depression, 1929–1933
sources.historical_claim: The Great Depression became a global economic and financial crisis, exposing severe weaknesses in banking and monetary systems and prompting major institutional changes.
sources.verification_status: Primary contemporary official record verified — Federal Reserve Board Annual Report 1933
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৯২৯–১৯৩৩ সালের মহামন্দা বৈশ্বিক অর্থনৈতিক ও আর্থিক সংকটে পরিণত হয় এবং ব্যাংকিং ও মুদ্রাব্যবস্থার গুরুতর দুর্বলতা প্রকাশ করে; এর পর বড় ধরনের প্রাতিষ্ঠানিক পরিবর্তন আসে।
sources.notes: The contemporary 1933 Federal Reserve Board Annual Report records successive banking difficulties from 1930 through March 1933 and states that nearly 5,500 banks suspended operations between December 1929 and February 1933. The report provides direct contemporary evidence for the banking-crisis phase of the Great Depression.
sources.primary_passage: Between the end of December 1929 and the end of February 1933 nearly 5,500 banks, or more than one bank in every five, suspended operations
sources.passage_locator: Annual Report of the Federal Reserve Board, 1933, section “Developments Leading to the Banking Crisis,” opening discussion of banking failures.

sources.title: Bank for International Settlements, 1930
sources.historical_claim: The 20 January 1930 Constituent Charter established the Bank for International Settlements and recorded its founding by the central banks of Belgium, France, Germany, Great Britain, Italy and Japan together with a US banking group.
sources.bn_historical_claim: ২০ জানুয়ারি ১৯৩০-এর কনস্টিটুয়েন্ট চার্টার ব্যাংক ফর ইন্টারন্যাশনাল সেটেলমেন্টস প্রতিষ্ঠা করে এবং বেলজিয়াম, ফ্রান্স, জার্মানি, গ্রেট ব্রিটেন, ইতালি ও জাপানের কেন্দ্রীয় ব্যাংকগুলোর সঙ্গে একটি মার্কিন ব্যাংকিং গোষ্ঠীর প্রতিষ্ঠায় অংশগ্রহণ নথিবদ্ধ করে।
sources.notes: Primary document identified and locked for this event; further archival comparison may add additional passages or context.
sources.primary_passage: Whereas the Powers signatory to the Hague Agreement of January, 1930, have adopted a Plan which contemplates the founding ... of an International Bank to be called the Bank for International Settlements
sources.passage_locator: Constituent Charter of the Bank for International Settlements, 20 January 1930, opening recital.

sources.title: Bretton Woods Conference, 1944
sources.historical_claim: The Articles of Agreement of the International Monetary Fund were adopted at the United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference at Bretton Woods on 22 July 1944, forming part of the Final Act of the conference.
sources.bn_historical_claim: ২২ জুলাই ১৯৪৪ ব্রেটন উডস সম্মেলনে আন্তর্জাতিক মুদ্রা তহবিলের Articles of Agreement গৃহীত হয় এবং তা সম্মেলনের Final Act-এর অংশ হয়।
sources.notes: Primary document identified and locked for this event; further archival comparison may add additional passages or context. Passage verified against the IMF's published Articles of Agreement; the IMF Archives also catalogs the 1944 Final Act containing the Articles.
sources.primary_passage: The International Monetary Fund is established and shall operate in accordance with the following provisions.
sources.passage_locator: Articles of Agreement of the International Monetary Fund, Introductory Article, adopted 22 July 1944.

sources.title: Banque de France nationalized, 1945
sources.historical_claim: Article 1 of France's Law No. 45-15 of 2 December 1945 provided that the Banque de France would be nationalized from 1 January 1946, with its shares transferred to the state.
sources.bn_historical_claim: ২ ডিসেম্বর ১৯৪৫-এর ফরাসি আইন নং ৪৫-১৫-এর ১ নম্বর অনুচ্ছেদে ১ জানুয়ারি ১৯৪৬ থেকে ব্যাংক দ্য ফ্রঁস জাতীয়করণ এবং এর শেয়ার রাষ্ট্রের মালিকানায় হস্তান্তরের বিধান করা হয়।
sources.notes: Primary document identified and locked for this event; further archival comparison may add additional passages or context.
sources.primary_passage: Les banques d'émission sont nationalisées
sources.passage_locator: French Law No. 45-15, 2 December 1945, nationalization provisions concerning banks of issue.

sources.title: Bank of England nationalized
sources.historical_claim: The Bank of England Act 1946 provided for the transfer of Bank stock to the Treasury and changed the Bank's ownership structure from private stockholding to state ownership.
sources.bn_historical_claim: ব্যাংক অব ইংল্যান্ড অ্যাক্ট ১৯৪৬ ব্যাংকের শেয়ার ট্রেজারিতে হস্তান্তরের বিধান করে এবং ব্যক্তিমালিকানাধীন শেয়ারহোল্ডিং থেকে রাষ্ট্রীয় মালিকানায় মালিকানা কাঠামো পরিবর্তন করে।
sources.notes: Primary institutional/legal document identified and locked for this event; additional archival passages can be added later where useful.
sources.primary_passage: the whole of the existing capital stock of the Bank ... shall, by virtue of this section, be transferred ... to such person as the Treasury may by order nominate, to be held by that person on behalf of the Treasury
sources.passage_locator: Bank of England Act 1946, section 1(1)(a).

sources.title: Nixon closes the gold window
sources.historical_claim: On 15 August 1971, President Richard Nixon announced the suspension of the dollar's convertibility into gold for foreign central banks and other reserve holders, marking a decisive break in the Bretton Woods monetary arrangement.
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৫ আগস্ট ১৯৭১ প্রেসিডেন্ট রিচার্ড নিক্সন বিদেশি কেন্দ্রীয় ব্যাংক ও অন্যান্য রিজার্ভ ধারকদের জন্য ডলারের স্বর্ণে রূপান্তরযোগ্যতা স্থগিত করার ঘোষণা দেন, যা ব্রেটন উডস মুদ্রাব্যবস্থার একটি निर्णায়ক বিচ্ছেদ ঘটায়।
sources.notes: The passage is directly verified in President Nixon's 15 August 1971 Address to the Nation, the primary presidential speech in which he announced the temporary suspension of dollar convertibility into gold or other reserve assets. The previous source URL pointed to an unrelated later report and has been corrected.
sources.primary_passage: I have directed the Secretary of the Treasury to suspend temporarily the convertibility of the dollar into gold or other reserve assets
sources.passage_locator: President Richard Nixon, Address to the Nation Outlining a New Economic Policy, 15 August 1971; directive announcing temporary suspension of dollar convertibility.

sources.title: Basel Committee established
sources.historical_claim: In December 1974, the G10 central-bank Governors established the Committee on Banking Regulations and Supervisory Practices after major international banking and currency disturbances, creating the institution that became the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision.
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৯৭৪ সালের ডিসেম্বরে আন্তর্জাতিক ব্যাংকিং ও মুদ্রাবাজারের গুরুতর অস্থিরতার পর G10 কেন্দ্রীয় ব্যাংকের গভর্নররা Committee on Banking Regulations and Supervisory Practices প্রতিষ্ঠা করেন, যা পরবর্তীতে Basel Committee on Banking Supervision হয়।
sources.notes: The BIS's 12 February 1975 contemporary media release records that the central-bank Governors of the Group of Ten countries and Switzerland had established a standing committee of experts on banking and foreign-exchange regulations and supervisory practices, under George Blunden. The BIS historical record dates the Governors' decision to December 1974, and the 1975 release is a near-contemporary official institutional record of the committee's establishment. This supports Grade A for the establishment claim, while the database should distinguish the December 1974 Governors' decision from the February 1975 public confirmation. The BIS's 12 February 1975 contemporary release directly confirms the committee's establishment; BIS history dates the Governors' decision to the end of 1974.
sources.primary_passage: have established a standing committee of experts on banking and foreign exchange regulations and supervisory practices
sources.passage_locator: BIS media release, 12 February 1975, confirming the standing committee established by the Group-of-Ten central-bank Governors.

sources.title: Plaza Accord
sources.historical_claim: The finance ministers and central-bank governors of France, Japan, the United Kingdom, the United States and West Germany agreed at the Plaza Hotel in New York in September 1985 to cooperate in promoting an orderly appreciation of major currencies against the US dollar.
sources.bn_historical_claim: ফ্রান্স, জাপান, যুক্তরাজ্য, যুক্তরাষ্ট্র ও পশ্চিম জার্মানির অর্থমন্ত্রীরা এবং কেন্দ্রীয় ব্যাংকের গভর্নররা সেপ্টেম্বর ১৯৮৫-তে নিউইয়র্কের প্লাজা হোটেলে প্রধান মুদ্রাগুলোর বিপরীতে মার্কিন ডলারের সুশৃঙ্খল অবমূল্যায়ন/অন্যান্য মুদ্রার মূল্যবৃদ্ধিতে সহযোগিতার জন্য একমত হন।
sources.notes: The 22 September 1985 Announcement of the Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors of France, Germany, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States is preserved as the contemporary Plaza statement. The text directly records the meeting, the five participating governments, and the agreed policy direction, including that further orderly appreciation of major nondollar currencies against the dollar was desirable and that the participants would cooperate to encourage it. The Federal Reserve's historical archive independently documents the Plaza Agreement and its subsequent foreign-exchange operations.
sources.primary_passage: further orderly appreciation of the major non-dollar currencies against the dollar is desirable
sources.passage_locator: Announcement of the Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors of France, Germany, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States, 22 September 1985.

sources.title: Basel I Capital Accord
sources.historical_claim: In July 1988, the G10 Governors approved the Basel Capital Accord, establishing an internationally coordinated framework for measuring bank capital and setting a target minimum capital ratio of 8% of risk-weighted assets for internationally active banks.
sources.bn_historical_claim: জুলাই ১৯৮৮-তে G10 গভর্নররা Basel Capital Accord অনুমোদন করেন, যা আন্তর্জাতিকভাবে সক্রিয় ব্যাংকগুলোর মূলধন পরিমাপের একটি সমন্বিত কাঠামো এবং ঝুঁকি-ওজনযুক্ত সম্পদের ৮% ন্যূনতম মূলধন অনুপাত নির্ধারণ করে।
sources.notes: Primary institutional/legal document identified and locked for this event; additional archival passages can be added later where useful.
sources.primary_passage: the total capital ratio must be no lower than 8% of risk-weighted assets
sources.passage_locator: International Convergence of Capital Measurement and Capital Standards, Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, July 1988; capital standard section.

sources.title: Asian financial crisis
sources.historical_claim: The Asian financial crisis began in Thailand in July 1997 after the baht was floated and spread across the region, producing severe financial and economic disruption and requiring international support programs.
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১৯৯৭ সালের জুলাইয়ে থাইল্যান্ডে বাত ভাসমান করার পর এশীয় আর্থিক সংকট শুরু হয় এবং অঞ্চলজুড়ে ছড়িয়ে পড়ে; এতে গুরুতর আর্থিক ও অর্থনৈতিক অস্থিরতা সৃষ্টি হয় এবং আন্তর্জাতিক সহায়তা কর্মসূচির প্রয়োজন হয়।
sources.notes: The 14 August 1997 Thailand Memorandum on Economic Policies, submitted in connection with the IMF-supported program, records the currency attacks, depletion of Bank of Thailand reserves, suspension of finance companies, and the float of the baht on 2 July 1997. The IMF's contemporaneous 2 July 1997 News Brief independently records Thailand's change to a managed float effective that date. The 20 August 1997 IMF approval release documents the subsequent stand-by arrangement and describes the spread of financial stress. These contemporary official records support the crisis-origin and international-assistance claims; broader claims about the crisis spreading across Asia should be treated as regional consequences rather than inferred solely from the Thai documents.
sources.primary_passage: the combination of a fixed exchange rate, an increasingly open capital account, and high domestic interest rates to combat inflation, attracted short-term capital flows that left the economy vulnerable to sudden shifts in market sentiment and external shocks.
sources.passage_locator: Thailand Memorandum on Economic Policies, 14 August 1997, section I, paragraph 1.

sources.title: European Central Bank established
sources.historical_claim: The European Central Bank was founded on 1 June 1998, replacing the European Monetary Institute and becoming the central institution of the Eurosystem and European System of Central Banks.
sources.bn_historical_claim: ১ জুন ১৯৯৮ ইউরোপীয় কেন্দ্রীয় ব্যাংক প্রতিষ্ঠিত হয়; এটি European Monetary Institute-এর স্থলাভিষিক্ত হয়ে ইউরোপীয় কেন্দ্রীয় ব্যাংকিং ব্যবস্থার কেন্দ্রীয় প্রতিষ্ঠান হয়।
sources.notes: The exact quoted wording is directly present in the ECB Annual Report 1998, section I, 'The establishment of the ECB', p. 129. The prior 9 June 1998 press-conference URL independently supports the date but did not match the stated passage locator as directly as the Annual Report; the passage source has therefore been aligned to the quoted document.
sources.primary_passage: the ECB was established on 1 June 1998
sources.passage_locator: ECB Annual Report 1998, section I, “The establishment of the ECB.”

sources.title: Global financial crisis
sources.historical_claim: The 2008 financial crisis became a global financial panic after the failure of Lehman Brothers in September 2008, prompting extraordinary central-bank liquidity and monetary-policy responses.
sources.bn_historical_claim: সেপ্টেম্বর ২০০৮-এ Lehman Brothers-এর পতনের পর ২০০৮ সালের আর্থিক সংকট একটি বৈশ্বিক আর্থিক আতঙ্কে রূপ নেয় এবং কেন্দ্রীয় ব্যাংকগুলোকে অস্বাভাবিক তারল্য ও মুদ্রানীতিগত ব্যবস্থা নিতে হয়।
sources.notes: The previous passage source pointed to a 15 September 2009 ECB speech, while the quoted wording is from the 14 October 2008 Joint Statement by Treasury, Federal Reserve, and FDIC. The source has been corrected to the official U.S. Treasury statement. The passage directly documents coordinated emergency measures; the broader claim about the crisis becoming global after Lehman's failure should remain supported separately.
sources.primary_passage: Today we are taking decisive actions to protect the U.S. economy, to strengthen public confidence in our financial institutions, and to foster the robust functioning of our credit markets.
sources.passage_locator: Joint Statement by Treasury, Federal Reserve, and FDIC, 14 October 2008; opening statement on coordinated crisis measures.
